question: A mine hoist's total is 8 times a shaft figure, and each shaft figure is 8 times the force on a single skip, because eight skips hang on every rope set. A skip has a mass of 46 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 9 times a number x, with 1 then added. That number x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 7 times x, plus 6, equals exactly 0. What is the mine hoist's total, in N?

An object's acceleration is calculated as 2 times the sum of 9 and 16, giving an effective velocity. A 44-kilogram object at this velocity develops kinetic energy as half mass times velocity squared. Add 7 Joules, subtract 16 Joules, multiply by 8, and convert from Joules to kilojoules. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

The number a drone team must report is a total energy budget in kJ, built as follows: the energy of motion of 8 identical drones, plus 22 kJ held in a spare battery pack, plus a further 26 kJ stored in the ground station's capacitor bank. Each drone has a mass of 14000 g and cruises at a speed, in m/s, equal to the number of different ways of choosing 2 waypoints out of 7. The hangar is kept at 18 °C throughout the test. Work out one drone's energy of motion and convert it to kJ before combining the 8 drones and then adding the two reserves in turn. What is the total budget, in kJ?
Integrating 3x^2 + 4x from 2 to 4 gives 56 m/s^2. A 71 kg mass produces force, decreased by 7, scaled by 7, converted to kN, decreased by 30. A threshold is 100 kN. What is the final force in kN?

The figure the crane display ends on is the kilonewton form of the force described below. A hoist controller takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0 and reads it as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A cage of mass 95 kg is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must apply to the cage is calculated. Because 4 identical cages hang from one beam the beam force is 4 times that value, a tare of 3 N from the load cell is then added, and a further 11 N of shackle weight is added after that. What figure does the crane display end on, in kN?

A cider works' plant figure is 8 times a line total, and a line total is 6 times a single crate's booked energy. A crate's booked energy is its kinetic energy plus 16 J drawn by the indexing motor. The crate has a mass of 13 kg, and its speed, in metres per second, is 3 times a base number. That base number is the largest whole number that divides both 286 and 400 exactly. What is the works' plant figure, in J?

A bearing works needs the total energy, in joules, held by all its test spindles at one instant. Two index rings on the rig carry 348 teeth and 271 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. Each test slider is run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number, and a slider has a mass of 15000 g. The energy one slider carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 5 sliders on a spindle. A rig holds 3 spindles, a bay holds 12 rigs, and the works has 8 identical bays. What total energy, in J, do the spindles hold?

A cable-drum test bench runs a loaded shuttle back and forth along a rail. The shuttle's speed v, in m/s, is the larger value that satisfies v^2 - 9v + 20 = 0. The shuttle has a mass of 15 kg, and the energy it carries by virtue of its motion is logged for each pass. The bench makes 8 passes in a run, and the log expresses a run's total in kilojoules. The site operates 9 identical benches, and the company owns 9 identical sites. What total energy, in kJ, does the company have in motion at that moment?
Choose 7 from 2: C(7,2) = 21. With 13 kg, force = 273 N, times 4, convert to 1.092 kN, minus 27. The material yield is 95%. What is the final force in kN?

The second derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 at x=2 is -4. After scaling by 8, a 107 kg component (or 107000 grams) produces force. After subtracting 11 and converting to kN, what is the final force in kilonewtons?

A rally team's energy sheet ends by adding 30 J for the starter motor and then subtracting 18 J for the telemetry unit. Before those two adjustments the sheet holds 6 times the kinetic energy of one test sled, because six sleds run the course together. Each sled has a mass of 57 kg, and the course is 250 m long. A sled's speed, in metres per second, is 7 times the largest whole number that divides both 75 and 91 exactly. What figure does the energy sheet end with, in J?

A mine shift boss wants the net force, in newtons, that a cart motor actually supplies. It is the force needed to accelerate an 89 kg cart, reduced by 27 N provided by a downhill grade and by a further 23 N from a tailwind in the tunnel. The cart's acceleration, in m/s², is 7 times the smaller root of x² - 7x + 6 = 0. What net force, in N, does the motor supply?

A load test uses stress polynomial x² - 14x + 48, selecting the larger root (8 m/s²). A 183 kg structure produces force, increased by 22 N for preload, converted to kN, increased by 24 kN for boost, then amplified 6 times. What is the total applied load in kN?

A 104,000 g sled on a rocket-sled track is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to 7 more than the number of ways to choose 2 sensors from a set of 12. The thrust required for this is converted to kN. The track runs 5 sleds per session and 9 sessions per week, so the weekly thrust tally is the single-sled value multiplied by 5 and then by 9. The track is 2 km long. What is the weekly tally, in kN?

A vibration laboratory fits the curve 3x^3 - 3x^2 to a recorded trace, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 3 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a test mass of 14 kg on the shaker. The bench records the energy the mass carries because of its motion, then subtracts a damping allowance of 25 J, a mounting allowance of 9 J, and finally adds a calibration offset of 3 J. The shaker head is 0.4 m across, a dimension the bench never uses. What number, in joules, does the bench report?

A sequence sum: (2*1-1) + (2*2-1) + ... + (2*7-1) = 49. A 41-kilogram mass at 49 m/s has kinetic energy. Convert to kilojoules, scale by 7, then 5, add 15. The mass identifier is P-2024, irrelevant. What is the energy in J?

Solving x^2 - 11*x + 24 = 0 gives the larger root as 8. A 157-kilogram object with acceleration 8 m/s^2 experiences force. Subtract 26, subtract 19, multiply by 5, and multiply by 7. What is the final force in newtons?
Solving x^2 - 11x + 28 = 0, the larger root (x=7) is picked. A 17 kg object produces force. After scaling by 8, adding 14, and converting to kN, what is the final force in kilonewtons?

A quadratic solver finds the larger root of x² - 10x + 21 = 0 (which is 7 m/s), then adds 3 for velocity 10 m/s. A 59 kg mass at 10 m/s yields energy, scaled by 9, reduced by 21 J, and converted to kilojoules. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A calibration sheet at a conveyor-belt test bench lists two candidate acceleration readings, in meters per second squared, for a gearbox housing: the two numbers add up to 8 and multiply together to give 15. The correct reading is the larger of the two, and subtracting 3 from it gives the actual acceleration of a housing with a mass of 106,000 grams. (The conveyor belt itself runs at 240 volts, a fact that plays no role here.) Find the push this housing requires, in newtons, then subtract 6 from that number. Convert what remains into kilonewtons, and then add 23 more. What is the final number, in kilonewtons?

A precision control system uses a 186 kg load. The greatest common divisor of specification values 141 and 224 (which is 1 m/s²) is scaled by 3 to yield 3 m/s² effective acceleration. Force is calculated, reduced by 21 N for baseline correction, then converted to kN. A tachometer reading 2500 rpm is unused. What is the final control force in kN?

A crane's hoist acceleration, in meters per second squared, equals 5 multiplied by the sum of 6 and 5. This acts on an 80,000 gram load block; find the resulting force, add 29 newtons for a cable-tension correction, convert the total to kilonewtons, subtract 17 kilonewtons for a counterweight offset, and multiply the result by 11 for an eleven-crane yard. A separate anemometer on site reads 22 km/h, which plays no part in this calculation. What is the final force, in kilonewtons, for the whole yard?

A packaging machine drives a carriage whose mass plate reads 21000 g. The control curve is y = 4x^3 + 2x^2, and the slope of that curve at x = 2 is found first; adding 21 to it gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to the carriage. The belt must supply the force that produces that acceleration, and 16 N of that force is absorbed by the tensioner and subtracted. Three carriages run on the machine, so the machine demand is 3 times the corrected single-carriage force. The log records the result in kilonewtons. What does the log record, in kN?

The total in a hoist report, in N, is 5 times a bay figure. The bay figure is 29 N less than the combined force of 4 identical hoists. Each hoist supplies the force needed to accelerate a 49,000 g load at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 8x + 7 = 0. The hoist cable is 12 m long. What is the total in the report, in N?

Integral of 3·x² from 1 to 4 is 63 m/s² acceleration. With 150 kg, force = 9450 N, reduced by 30, scaled by 11, increased by 7, scaled by 6. The record ID is 1001, not used. What is the final force in Newtons?
